 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team has had to get by without star forward David Mirkovic for the start of the season, and they will have to continue to do so for some time.
 The sophomore spent the end of the summer rehabbing from August foot surgery and was not going to be available for the early going. But a surprise appendectomy just before the season opener further clouded his recovery , making it nearly impossible to gauge when Illinois could have one of their most important players back out there on the court.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement At the end of last week, two important details emerged regarding Mirkovic and his recovery. First was that he was out of a walking boot for the first time since foot surgery. Second was that following a Thursday check-in appointment, he would begin the "procedure process" of ramping up to playing shape. At that stage, this included shooting a basketball.
 Head coach Brad Underwood had additional updates on these two simultaneous rehabs on Monday, providing more color on what he is doing now and what they need to see before considering a return to practice and eventually games.
 "Every day is a step, every day is a step closer to him being back in uniform," Underwood said. "I watched him shoot today, and he's not back practicing. He's back lifting weights after the appendix, which is a great thing."

Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images
 Latest on Rehabbing David Mirkovic
 While getting back in the weight room is a big step fresh off of appendix surgery, Underwood makes clear that Mirkovic has not returned to practice and there remains no concrete timeline for him to get there. Being that he hasn't played or worked out in several months, the first step will be regaining the strength and conditioning necessary to start in high-intensity games.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I think the one thing we all got to understand is we're 14 or 15 weeks removed from a lot of physical activity, and the appendix set him back in the weight room," Underwood outlined. "We're not going to bring him back until he's close to 100 percent... until he's practicing with our guys, until there's some comfort out there."
 Nov 2, 2026; Champaign, Illinois, USA; Illinois Fighting Illini head coach Brad Underwood talks with player guard Blake Fagbemi (8) during the second half against the Fairleigh Dickinson Knights at State Farm Center. Mandatory Credit: Ron Johnson-Imagn Images
 Illinois opened the season as the No. 3 ranked team but clearly hasn't been the same without the dynamic forward. After dropping an early road game to Texas Tech, the Illini came in as the nation's 10th ranked squad ahead of a huge matchup at Duke on Tuesday night.
 While it's not an ideal scenario, Underwood believes there are some positives that could come out of navigating the early part of the schedule without Mirkovic.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "It's a step by step, and do you wish you had David? Yes, we do. But we don't, and there's a lot of benefits to our team not having him right now and going through the rigors that we're going through playing the schedule that we're playing."
 After facing Duke, Illinois hosts three-straight non-conference games against Eastern Illinois, Winthrop, and Western Kentucky before welcoming in another high-profile opponent in UConn on December 4th. It would appear that Mirkovic has an uphill battle to climb to be considered available at that stage, but as Underwood points out, it could be a great opportunity to learn what this team is all about in his stead.
